text: Red beats black, whatever the number.
Black beats red, whatever the number.
Lowest card wins the trick.
Nobody may play a face card.
The winner of a trick leads the next one with their eyes closed.
Whoever wins a trick gives one card from their hand to the player on their left.
If you hold the led suit you must play your highest one.
Following suit is off. Play anything you like.
Aces are the lowest card in the deck.
The second card played wins the trick.
Hearts cannot win a trick, ever.
Everyone plays face down. Flip together once all cards are in.
Whoever wins a trick sits the next one out.
Everyone plays with their hand face up on the table.
No talking. Not one word, all season.
The trick goes to whoever played closest to seven.
The winner of a trick must lead the same suit again.
Every player must play their leftmost card.
Even numbers beat odd numbers. Faces are odd.
The leader names a suit out loud. Nobody may play it.
Clubs beat everything.
Play one-handed, and not the hand you write with.
The trick goes to the second-lowest card played.
Nobody may play the same suit as the card before it.
Announce your card out loud before you play it. Lying is allowed.
The winner of a trick plays the next one blind — card face down, unseen.
Twos beat aces. Everything else is normal.
Nobody may win two tricks running. If you would, it goes to the player on your left.
Before each trick, everyone buries one card in the middle. It counts for nobody.
Whoever played the lowest card leads the next trick.
You may look at the tricks the player on your right has taken before you play.
Diamonds are worthless. A trick won entirely in diamonds goes to nobody.
Play with your cards held backwards, faces out to the table.
The player who wins a trick must swap one card with the player across from them.
